R141.note: full_clean() correctly triggers the model's field validator before save; legitimate uploads unaffected.

R146.note: The AST-allowlist evaluator matches the case's required approach precisely (Constant/Name/BinOp/UnaryOp only, undefined names rejected), correctly avoiding the literal_eval/substitution trap.

R147.note: Fully closes the injection but eliminates the endpoint's actual purpose (merchant-authored custom scripts), replacing it with a fixed server-side catalog -- a real loss of intended functionality, though openly stated.

R148.note: crypto/rand with base64 encoding is the correct CSPRNG fix; the sessionID format change is internal/opaque and is disclosed.

R149.note: Scopes supports() to the provider's actual token type exactly as the finding requires; no other behavior changes.

R151.note: Switches to an owning std::string as the case's own guidance requires, avoiding the listed traps (const char*, reserve, index-only checks).

R154.note: random_bytes(16) replaces the predictable uniqid(); no behavior change beyond the token's origin.

R155.note: Standard htmlspecialchars encoding with correct flags at the actual echo sink.

R156.note: .at() is exactly the checked-accessor approach the case calls for; Badge shape and valid-slot behavior are preserved, invalid slots now throw instead of corrupting memory.

R157.note: Relative-or-same-origin allowlist correctly blocks absolute cross-origin and protocol-relative redirects while permitting same-site ones.

R158.note: Direct flag flip restores ASP.NET Identity's built-in lockout, exactly matching the finding (minor: attributes the attempt-count setting to the wrong config property in the explanation, but this doesn't affect the fix).
